Split, trim and remap Bezier curves

Source: R/bezier.R
partial_bezier_points.Rd

Helpers that operate on the control points of Bezier curves, given as an n x 3 matrix with one control point per row (4 rows for a cubic curve).

Usage

partial_bezier_points(points, a, b)

split_bezier(points, t)

subdivide_bezier(points, n_divisions)

bezier_remap(bezier_tuples, new_number_of_curves)

Arguments

points

Control points, an n x 3 matrix (one row per point).

a, b

Start and end of the parameter interval.

t

Parameter at which to split.

n_divisions

Number of pieces.

bezier_tuples

Control points of the curves to remap, a 4k x 3 matrix.

new_number_of_curves

Number of curves in the result.

Value

A matrix of control points, one row per point.

Details

  • partial_bezier_points() returns the control points of the portion of the curve with parameter in [a, b], 0 <= a < b <= 1.

  • split_bezier() splits the curve at t and returns the control points of both halves stacked (2 n rows). Like upstream, a line (2 points) gives 4 rows p0, m, m, p1 and a single point gives 2 rows.

  • subdivide_bezier() splits the curve into n_divisions pieces of equal parameter length and returns their control points stacked (n_divisions * n rows). For curves of degree 4 or more, upstream's fallback splits at the wrong parameters (1/3 and 1/2 for three pieces); manimR splits at i / n_divisions, as upstream documents.

  • bezier_remap() takes a path of k cubic curves (a 4k x 3 matrix) and subdivides its curves so the result has new_number_of_curves curves, which must be at least k. Upstream takes a (k, 4, 3) array; here the curves are stacked rows as everywhere in manimR.

Examples

cubic <- rbind(c(0, 0, 0), c(1, 2, 0), c(3, -1, 0), c(4, 1, 0))
split_bezier(cubic, 0.5)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,] 0.00 0.00    0
#> [2,] 0.50 1.00    0
#> [3,] 1.25 0.75    0
#> [4,] 2.00 0.50    0
#> [5,] 2.00 0.50    0
#> [6,] 2.75 0.25    0
#> [7,] 3.50 0.00    0
#> [8,] 4.00 1.00    0
partial_bezier_points(cubic, 0.25, 0.75)
#>         [,1]    [,2] [,3]
#> [1,] 0.90625 0.71875    0
#> [2,] 1.59375 0.78125    0
#> [3,] 2.40625 0.21875    0
#> [4,] 3.09375 0.28125    0
nrow(subdivide_bezier(cubic, 3))
#> [1] 12
nrow(bezier_remap(Square()$points, 7))
#> [1] 28
